title: Neural citation recommendation with graph context
abstract: We propose a graph neural network for recommending scientific papers using citation context and document abstracts.

title: Citation recommendation using transformer encoders
abstract: This paper studies transformer encoders for matching citation contexts with relevant scientific publications.

title: Graph convolutional networks for scholarly recommendation
abstract: We combine graph convolutional networks with textual representations to improve scholarly paper recommendation.

title: Large language models for literature review generation
abstract: We evaluate large language models for generating related work sections and suggesting academic references.

title: Retrieval augmented generation for scientific question answering
abstract: This work studies retrieval augmented generation systems for scientific question answering with cited evidence.

title: Measuring citation bias in language model recommendations
abstract: We analyze whether language models prefer highly cited papers when asked to recommend scientific references.

title: Open science and responsible research metrics
abstract: We discuss transparent research assessment and responsible use of citation indicators in scholarly evaluation.

title: The Matthew effect in scientific citations
abstract: This paper models cumulative advantage and preferential attachment in the accumulation of scientific citations.

title: Gender imbalance in neuroscience reference lists
abstract: We measure gender imbalance in reference lists and compare observed citations with expected citation rates.

title: AI assisted writing in scientific publications
abstract: We estimate the use of AI assisted writing tools in scientific papers after the release of ChatGPT.

title: Foundation models for scientific discovery
abstract: We examine foundation models as tools for scientific search synthesis and discovery workflows.

title: Scientific impact and citation networks over time
abstract: We study how citation networks evolve and how prior visibility influences future scientific impact.
